name: rsync
description: Protects against destructive rsync operations like --delete and its variants.

destructive_patterns.name: rsync-delete
destructive_patterns.description: rsync --delete removes destination files not present in source.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The --delete flag removes files from the destination that don't exist in the \ source. If source and destination are swapped, or if the source is unexpectedly \ empty, important data on the destination can be permanently deleted.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - rsync --dry-run --delete: Preview what would be deleted \ - rsync without --delete: Only adds/updates, never deletes \ - rsync --backup --delete: Keep backup copies of deleted files

destructive_patterns.name: rsync-del-short
destructive_patterns.description: rsync --del is a short alias for --delete and is destructive.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The --del flag is shorthand for --delete-during, which deletes destination files \ not present in source during the transfer. This is slightly more dangerous than \ --delete-after because deletions happen incrementally.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - rsync --dry-run --del: Preview deletions first \ - rsync without deletion flags: Additive sync only \ - Use --delete-after for predictable batch deletion
